2.3.9.1 KO
 CCP monitoring for the sous vide process in the production kitchen area (= small-volume production for bulk consumers/catering customers) is not under sufficient control; compliance with the defined CCP criteria cannot be conclusively demonstrated:
 According to internal specifications (=CCP3 definition; version25/status 27/06/2025), sous vide finished goods/products produced in the company must reach a product-specific defined minimum heating temperature as part of CCP monitoring (e.g. for chicken fillet sous vide >62°C or octopus sous vide >72°C), which must then be maintained for a product-specific minimum time (e.g. for chicken fillet sous vide > 2 hours or for octopus sous vide >16 hours); the product must then be cooled to below 10°C core temperature within a maximum of 2 hours. The product-specific requirements in this regard can be found in the document Overview of core temperatures 4_AA_#0498 (V1/10.07.2024).
 
 The company produces sous-vide products in two different production areas, in the so-called ‘large scale’ area where large quantities/volumes of sous-vide products are produced, which are primarily marketed as pre-packaged products in the food retail trade. For the sous-vide products produced here in industrial cooking cabinets, compliance with the relevant CCP criteria can be demonstrated in a traceable manner via electronic temperature/time records (=recording of heating temperature, holding time and cooling temperature with cooling times).
 To date, this has not been the case for small-batch sous vide production in the production kitchen, which is intended for bulk consumers/catering customers. Here, for each sous vide production batch in a conventional manual cooking cabinet (without automatic temperature/time recording), only the time at which the product reached the specified heating temperature is recorded; the re-cooling time required for the product to cool to a core temperature of less than 10°C after the heating process is also documented. The CCP test record described does not show that the product-specific holding time required by the CCP criterion has been complied with; there are also no other ways of checking whether the product-specific temperature-holding time parameter, which is decisive for product safety, has been complied with. Furthermore, the cooling time is not consistently traceable; only the required period is specified, not the beginning and end of the cooling time.

CCP monitoring is carried out at the beginning, middle, and end of the day or in the event of a format change by performing an ejection test of the inspector with this test bottle.
 
 During the test requested in the field audit of 07/22/25 (test on the 1 L format), the operator used a test bottle with a volume of added water that was visually much greater than 10 ml and was deemed compliant by the HEUFT inspector. It was therefore requested that the test be redone with the 10 ml dose as planned. Three tests were thus redone and each time deemed non-compliant by the HEUFT inspector (the test bottle was not detected by the inspector as it should have been).  The metal detector monitoring procedure in the picking area was not correctly applied to detect any loss of control of the metal detector CCP in a timely manner. During the audit, the operator in charge of the control retrieved the carton before it was properly ejected. A DPM verification test was carried out, and the ejector did not eject the cartons onto the NC product ejection ramp. The EN-EXP-004 record does not provide for recording the proper functioning of the ejector, so it is not possible to demonstrate when the ejector stopped working. 
 Work instruction IT/QUAL/006 specifies that in the event of a failure to eject, the products must be blocked. The operator on duty indicated that the ejector was not working properly when production started in the morning. The procedure was not followed.
 In addition, the stainless steel indicator was not detected by the DPM and when two successive indicators passed, the second indicator was not detected. 
 The CCP DPM is therefore not under control. A KO is established for this requirement.
